title: NCERT Grade 10 Mathematics | Image | Page 13
text:
[IMAGE] This image illustrates the concept of **similar triangles and centroids** within a triangle, often used to explain properties of triangles and their medians.

The diagram shows a large triangle \( \triangle PQR \) with a smaller, inner triangle \( \triangle DEF \) formed by connecting the midpoints of its sides. Point \( O \) represents the **centroid** of \( \triangle PQR \), which is the point where all three medians (lines from each vertex to the midpoint of the opposite side) intersect. The medians are shown as \( PD \), \( QE \), and \( RF \), and they divide the triangle into six smaller triangles of equal area. This helps in understanding the properties of centroids and the division of triangles into smaller congruent parts.
Source: NCERT Grade 10 Mathematics, Page 13

The diagram shows a semicircle with a triangle inscribed in it, where the diameter of the semicircle acts as the hypotenuse of the triangle. title: NCERT Grade 10 Mathematics | Image | Page 2
text:
[IMAGE] This image illustrates the concept of the **angle of elevation** in trigonometry. It shows a scenario where an observer looks up at an object (like a mountain peak) from a certain point on the ground. The labeled parts include the **line of sight** (the imaginary straight line from the observer’s eye to the object), the **angle of elevation** (the angle formed between the line of sight and the horizontal level), and the **horizontal level** (a reference line parallel to the ground). This concept is used to determine heights and distances using trigonometric ratios like sine, cosine, and tangent.
Source: NCERT Grade 10 Mathematics, Page 2

title: NCERT Grade 10 Mathematics | Image | Page 2
text:

The labeled parts include the **horizontal level** (a reference line at the observer's eye level), the **line of sight** (the imaginary line connecting the observer's eye to the object), and the **angle of depression** (the angle formed between the horizontal level and the line of sight when looking downward). This concept helps in understanding how to measure angles below the horizontal plane, often used in solving real-world problems involving heights and distances.
